prize_parts.citation: For the development of palladium-catalysed carbon-nitrogen cross-coupling

statement.case_for: Palladium-catalysed C-N cross-coupling is a general, original and fully mature synthetic method. The ligand-controlled Buchwald and Hartwig protocols made aryl amines routinely accessible, and the reaction is now a daily tool in pharmaceutical, agrochemical and materials synthesis. It has three decades of independent confirmation, a well-understood mechanism and successive ligand generations. The 2010 prize covered C-C coupling (Heck, Negishi, Suzuki) and did not address C-N bond formation. Attribution is also the cleanest on the list: two groups developed the catalytic, general version independently and in parallel, which fits a two-person prize with a precise citation.
statement.case_against: The strongest objection is proximity to the 2010 cross-coupling prize. Some members may see C-N coupling as a downstream extension of an area already honoured. Kosugi's earlier tin-amide work, and Migita-type precedent, leave a small priority wrinkle. The topic also drew little first-place support in the openings, where targeted protein degradation (B057) was clearly the broadest favourite, so a B068 prize would have to win on rigour and clean attribution, not on breadth of support.

responses.point: Somfai ranked B068 first, arguing that C-N coupling is among the most widely used bond constructions, that Buchwald and Hartwig are the natural independent pair, and that Kosugi is a minor wrinkle.
responses.response: I agree on the scientific and attribution case and on the point that the 2010 prize did not cover C-N coupling. I would qualify the claim that Kosugi is only a minor wrinkle. His tin-amide coupling is a real precedent, and the citation should say 'development of the catalytic, ligand-controlled, general method' so the credit stays precise and defensible. I still do not think this justifies adding him, because the general catalytic method is what changed practice.

responses.point: Aqvist ranked Car-Parrinello (B037) first and called B068 excellent chemistry, but raised the 2010 overlap and the Migita priority question.
responses.response: I take the 2010 concern seriously, but I disagree that it counts heavily against B068. The 2010 prize rewarded a specific class of C-C bond formation, and C-N coupling needed new ligand design and mechanism. I do not rank B037 on the shortlist as high, because it drew only one first-place vote and no other ranking. I accept that Car-Parrinello is unambiguous in attribution and is a fair candidate for a later computational prize. On Migita, we have no evidence that his work reached general catalytic C-N coupling, so I would not alter the credited names.

responses.point: Linke, the chair, ranked B057 first. He sees induced proximity as a conceptual shift that also explains thalidomide-type drugs, with extensive confirmation across labs.
responses.response: I share the view that B057 is the most important new idea on the list, and that is why I ranked it second. My reservations are about allocation and timing. A three-name cap forces a choice among Crews, Deshaies, Handa, Ciulli, Gray and others. The PROTAC and molecular-glue lineages are different discoveries, and no degrader has been approved. A two-part prize could split them, but that would need more than three people. B068 asks the committee to settle none of these questions, so I prefer it as a first choice, and I would support B057 if the committee is persuaded that the clinical evidence is sufficient.

responses.point: Chabes ranked B057 first with Crews, Deshaies and Handa. He argues that the molecular-glue mechanism explains the thalidomide puzzle and that three names span concept and mechanism.
responses.response: The Handa cereblon result is a decisive mechanistic discovery, and I accept that Crews, Deshaies and Handa span concept and mechanism better than a Ciulli-based trio. But this trio leaves out Ciulli's VHL ligands and structural basis, and Gray's and Sakamoto's contributions, so some of the credit disagreement stays open. A configuration of this kind is less settled than the two-person B068 case, and I would want that discussed explicitly.

uncertainties: Whether the committee will treat C-N coupling as too close to the 2010 cross-coupling prize.
Whether clinical evidence for degraders is now sufficient for B057, and how credit would be allocated between PROTACs and molecular glues within three names.
Whether Kosugi's tin-amide precursor needs any acknowledgement in the citation.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict with any shortlisted candidate is apparent from the provided profile. I am a Stockholm University colleague of the Secretary, Peter Brzezinski, but none of the shortlisted nominees is connected to Stockholm University or to my own work in electron crystallography.
